summary: Every SOP rule the shipped package breaks (fitted intercept, mean of blank results, excluding non-detect blanks, subtracting the blank before dilution, flags on the corrected reading, inclusive CCV pass on the rounded recovery, two-sided bracketing, spike recovery without dilution) has a dedicated family whose full-report comparison rejects the shipped or a plausible partial fix. The shipped fallbacks the contract says to keep (no blank results, unbracketed runs, non-detect spike recovery) are also covered. The comparator accepts any blank_levels key order and int/float values, and it applies exactly the documented tolerance. I found no false rejection or accepted wrong path.
checks_performed: Mapped each shipped defect to the fixture that exposes it (static hand traces, not executed). calib.py:14 has no intercept; calibration.jsonl rows 3-4 and section_one_limits row 6 have nonzero or negative intercepts. blanks.py:6-9 uses the first blank; blank_mean row 1 gives mean 3.5, first blank 2.0 and median 3.0. blank_nondetects row 1 gives 2.5 when non-detect blanks are excluded and 1.0 when they are included. samples.py:9 computes reading*dil-level; dilution.jsonl gives 52.5 versus 18.0 for W-72. samples.py:13-17 flags on the amount; in flag_basis W-81 is ND rather than J and W-82 is J rather than blank. calibration row 4 W-25 is J with value 26. qc.py:9 uses a strict, unrounded check; ccv_limits CCV-1 is 90.0 and CCV-3 is 110.04, both pass. qc.py:12-17 uses the previous CCV only; ccv_bracketing W-111 lies between a pass and a fail and expects false. qc.py:21 divides by added*dilution; spike_recovery row 2 expects 380 rather than 47.5.

Traced the contract fallbacks ('keep the calculation the code makes today'). blank_no_results rows 2-4 expect the first blank reading when every blank is a non-detect, and row 1 expects 0.0 when there are no blanks. ccv_unbracketed expects true before the first CCV and the previous CCV's pass after the last CCV. spike_nondetects expects the shipped added*dilution denominator on SOP-defined amounts (48.75, -16.04, -15.0, 52.5). report_order row 1 B-SPK As/Cd confirms the ND-parent path uses the dilution denominator, while Tl (both results) does not.

Checked plausible wrong alternatives against the fixtures. A fit that averages replicates or regresses conc on response is caught by calibration row 3. Ignoring per-standard is_counts is caught by calibration row 4. Clamping readings to zero is caught by negative_readings rows 1-2. Blank-subtracting CCVs is caught by report_order row 1 (Tl blank 0.625, recovery 100). The next CCV only, or the first/last CCV of the batch, is caught by ccv_bracketing W-112 and W-111. The nearest CCV on either side for unbracketed runs is caught by ccv_unbracketed row 4 (W-128). Treating an ND parent as zero is caught by spike_nondetects. Alphabetical analyte order and sorted run ids are caught by report_order rows 1-2.

Checked the comparator in tests/test_outputs.py:119-142. Number tolerance matches instruction.md:7 (relative 1e-6 when |e|>=1, otherwise absolute 1e-6). Booleans are rejected as numbers. Exact type and equality are required for id, analyte, flag, ccv_ok, pass and null values. blank_levels is compared by key set, so its order is free. List lengths and order are exact, as instruction.md:7 and reduction-sop.md:114 require.

Checked boundary numerics against the SOP section-1 margins. flag_limits values sit about 1.5e-5 or more from mdl/loq. ccv_limits recoveries sit 0.01 or more from a rounding tie. Exact-on-limit cases (<= vs <) are excluded by reduction-sop.md:39-42, so the verifier need not distinguish them.

Checked the execution path. The verifier installs its own driver copy (test_outputs.py:52-63) and runs python3 -I -S as uid 65534 against /app/src (test_outputs.py:78-116). test.sh:16 makes /app readable. The byte-identity check on the delivered driver matches instruction.md:3.
Checked roster pinning and row counts (test_outputs.py:66-75), and that the capacity test asserts 80 runs, 4 analytes and 8 standards (test_outputs.py:219-223).

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails if missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: Each SOP section 2-8 rule has a named family that compares the complete report. A static trace of the shipped package shows each family fails on the corresponding defect.

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result (values, membership, uniqueness, required outputs)
coverage_sweep.reason: compare() checks the top-level key set, blank_levels keys and values, and every entry's exact key set, values and types in each of samples, ccvs and spikes, with exact list lengths.

coverage_sweep.category: Named domain rule has an isolating case whose outcome changes when the rule is wrong
coverage_sweep.reason: Each rule has an isolating case: fitted intercept (calibration rows 3-4), mean of results anywhere (blank_mean), ND blanks excluded (blank_nondetects), blank before dilution (dilution), flag on corrected reading (flag_basis), limits (flag_limits), no clamping (negative_readings), rounded inclusive CCV (ccv_limits), two-sided bracketing (ccv_bracketing), spike recovery vs added (spike_recovery). Each fixture is built so that only the named rule changes the result.

Traced the partial fixes listed in checks_performed (replicate averaging, inverse regression, clamping, blank-subtracted CCVs, one-sided or nearest bracketing, ND-as-zero recovery, sorted output). Each changes at least one compared field in a named fixture.

coverage_sweep.category: Contract-valid alternatives accepted (formatting, ordering, implementation choices)
coverage_sweep.reason: Output is parsed with json.loads, not compared as text. blank_levels key order is free, and int/float are both accepted. The tolerance absorbs differences between OLS formulations. Rounding-method differences cannot matter because SOP 1 excludes ties within 1e-6. Exact-on-limit comparisons are excluded by the section-1 margins. The driver's -I -S isolation affects only non-stdlib imports; the contract grades /app/src run through the verifier's driver copy, and the environment has no third-party numeric packages.

coverage_sweep.category: Documented restrictions and lifecycle behavior enforced
coverage_sweep.reason: The requirement to leave the driver unchanged is enforced by the byte comparison on the pre-install bytes. The 'no added correction/qualifier/exclusion' restriction is enforced through exact flags and values; for example, a ND-as-zero or clamping addition fails. The shipped fallbacks the contract says to keep are graded by blank_no_results, ccv_unbracketed and spike_nondetects.

coverage_sweep.category: Initialization-to-first-event transition of state machines (CCV bracketing)
coverage_sweep.reason: Runs before the first CCV (W-121, W-128 after a failing CCV-25), batches with no CCV (ccv_unbracketed row 3) and runs after the last CCV (W-123 pass, W-125/W-125S fail) are all graded.

coverage_sweep.category: Signed derived quantities: sign partitions discriminated
coverage_sweep.reason: Covered sign cases: negative and positive blank levels (blank_no_results row 2, negative_readings row 1, generated-1 row 4), negative intercept (section_one_limits row 6), negative readings down to -1e4 (negative_readings row 2), and negative and positive spike recoveries (spike_recovery row 3, spike_nondetects row 1).

coverage_sweep.category: Proxy behavior, Oracle-specific representation, stale binaries, self-controlled comparisons, unreachable cases
coverage_sweep.reason: Expected reports are roster-pinned files owned by the verifier, not candidate-derived. The verifier installs its own driver before running. No compiled artifact is reused. The hand-traced fixtures fall inside the section-1 limits. Values compared are semantic JSON values, not native encoding.
There is one test per SOP rule family, and assertion messages name the family, batch index, section, entry id/analyte and key.

rules: SOP 5 blank subtracted before dilution and flag on corrected reading
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: flag_basis row 2: blank level 2.0 with dilution 100 gives corrected 0.5 (ND), where the shipped amount-based flag would give J or blank. W-85 gives corrected 4.5 (J) with value 9.

rules: SOP 4 blank level / instruction fallback to shipped calculation
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: blank_no_results rows 2-4: every blank is ND, so the level is the first blank's reading (-1.0, 0.25, 0.5). The subsequent J flags depend on that level.

rules: SOP 3 ND fallback plus SOP 5 amounts
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: spike_nondetects row 2 and report_order row 1 B-SPK use an ND parent with a nonzero blank level and dilution. Expected recovery uses the SOP amount with the shipped denominator. Tl (both results) uses the SOP denominator without dilution.
In report_order row 1, A-CCV fails for Tl and Pb but passes for As and Cd. The bracketed Z-9/B-SPK and the after-last C-1 carry per-analyte ccv_ok values.
report_order row 1 has a Tl blank level of 0.625 and a Z-CCV Tl recovery of 100.0. A blank-subtracted CCV would report 98.75 and fail the recovery comparison.

rules: SOP 8 list order follows run order and analytes order
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: report_order uses non-alphabetical analyte order (Tl, As, Pb, Cd), standards whose conc keys are ordered differently from analytes, and unsorted run ids (Z-9, B-SPK, C-1).

section_one_limits row 8 (added 0.001, recovery about 100 at 1e-4 tolerance) and row 3 (intercept 1e4*slope with dilution 1000). Cancellation error is far below tolerance for any standard OLS formulation.
